title: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) successfully concludes Special Campaign 6
body_text: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has successfully concluded Special Campaign 6, conducted from 2nd to 31st October 2026, with active participation of MoSPI's field offices across various States and Union Territories as well as the subordinate offices, attached and autonomous offices spread across the country, with notable achievements. During the campaign, cleanliness drives and other related activities as mandated were organized. The progress of the campaign was regularly monitored by the Secretary, MoSPI and achievements were uploaded on a day-to-day basis on the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) Portal. Key Achievements of Special Campaign 6.0 (i)  Disposal of Pending Matters: The Ministry disposed of 48 Public Grievances and 9 Public Grievance Appeals. Efforts were also undertaken to address and expedite references received from Members of Parliament (MPs) and matters relating to Parliamentary Assurances. (ii)  Efficient File Management: A total of 718 physical files were reviewed, of which 433 files were weeded out. Additionally, 1,607 e-files were reviewed and 1,522 e-files were closed, contributing to improved records management and administrative efficiency. (iii)  Space Management: A total of 1,982 sq. ft. of office space was freed through effective space-management initiatives. (iv)  Revenue Generation: Disposal of e-waste and scrap generated revenue of ₹3,69,819, promoting better utilisation of resources. (v)  Cleanliness and Environmental Improvement: 114 Cleanliness drives were conducted, promoting workplace hygiene and environmental sustainability. (vi)  Plantation drives were conducted to promote clean and green spaces in office premises. (vii)  Felicitation ceremony to recognize and appreciate the housekeeping staff for their hard work, dedication and invaluable contribution towards maintaining a clean, hygienic and well-organised workplace. 'Waste to Art' campaigns were conducted in the Field offices to promote reuse and recycling initiatives. Special One-Day Event As part of the campaign, MoSPI organised a dedicated One-Day Cleanliness Drive on 7th October 2026 across the Ministry and its attached and subordinate offices. Activities included cleanliness and plantation drives, waste segregation, e-waste management and space optimisation. The Field Operations Division (FOD) conducted cleanliness activities at around 53 sites across the country, while other offices undertook similar initiatives at their respective locations. The successful conclusion of Special Campaign 6 reflects the Ministry's continued commitment to cleanliness, efficient administration, environmental sustainability and the timely disposal of pending matters.
